Chapter 8.4

What Are Some Applications of Atomic Technologies and the Possible Issues That Can Arise from Them?

What we build with atoms, and what we have to decide about it

The same knowledge of atoms gives us a scan that finds a broken bone and a weapon that flattens a city. What do we do with that?

Learning Objectives

What you will be able to do by the end

1Describe how knowledge of atoms is used to make new materials.
2Give examples of atomic technologies used in medicine.
3Describe how nuclear energy is used to generate electricity.
4Discuss the social and ethical issues that arise from these applications.

Core concept

How is knowledge of atoms used to make new materials?

Scientists constantly seek to find out more about atoms as they try to create new materials from them.

Learn
  • Scientists constantly seek to find out more about atoms as they try to create new materials from them.Once you know how atoms behave, you can start designing materials on purpose rather than finding them by luck.
  • Gold-plated orchids exist in Singapore today because a local biochemist managed to coat living plant material with gold atoms.A real flower is picked and then covered in a layer of gold atoms so thin that the shape of every petal survives.
  • This works because the properties of the atoms being used are understood well enough to control where they go.Getting a metal to settle evenly over something as delicate as a petal takes knowing exactly how those atoms behave.
  • The creation of novel drugs and materials can serve as solutions to existing problems.New material, new answer to an old problem. That is the reason this research is funded.
Key Facts
  • Knowledge of atoms allows new materials to be created, such as living plant material coated with gold atoms.
  • An awareness of technological advances allows us to appreciate scientific developments.
Test

What makes a gold-plated orchid an example of atomic technology?

📓Now complete your notes: Section A: New materials from atomsComplete the gold-plated orchid example in the Take Note! box.
Core concept

How are atoms used in medicine?

The knowledge of atoms has been used for medical purposes, in treatment and in imaging.

The same hand, two ways of seeing it2 states
1Tap each button to switch between the two images of the same hand.
Tap a button to switch between the two views.
Learn
  • The knowledge of atoms has been used for medical purposes and to provide nuclear energy.The same understanding turns up in a hospital and in a power station, doing completely different jobs.
  • In the field of medicine, the properties of atoms are applied in radiation therapy to cure diseases.Carefully aimed radiation can destroy diseased cells inside the body without the surgeon having to open it.
  • They are also applied in medical imaging, which includes magnetic resonance imaging, or MRI, and X-ray.Imaging means making a picture of the inside of the body without cutting into it.
  • Radiation from the X-ray machine is able to penetrate the skin and bones of the human body.The radiation passes straight through the soft parts and is stopped more by bone, which is what makes the bones show up pale.
  • Such radiation is given off by atoms that have large amounts of energy.The energy has to come from somewhere, and it comes from the atoms themselves.
Key Facts
  • In medicine, the properties of atoms are applied in radiation therapy to cure diseases, and in medical imaging including MRI and X-ray.
  • Radiation from the X-ray machine is able to penetrate the skin and bones of the human body.
  • Such radiation is given off by atoms that have large amounts of energy.
Test

Why do bones appear pale on an X-ray image while soft tissue does not?

📓Now complete your notes: Section B: Atoms in medicineComplete the two medical applications in the Take Note! box.
Application

What does a radiographer actually do?

A radiographer is a healthcare professional who uses medical radiation equipment to produce images of the human body.

Learn
  • A radiographer is a healthcare professional who uses medical radiation equipment to produce images of the human body.It is a job, and a common one. Every hospital needs people trained to run this equipment safely.
  • These images help doctors to diagnose any illness or injury in a patient.The radiographer takes the picture. The doctor reads it and decides what is wrong.
  • We may get an X-ray done if we break a bone or visit a dentist.Most people meet this technology for the first time in a dentist's chair rather than in a research laboratory.
Key Facts
  • A radiographer uses medical radiation equipment to produce images of the human body, which help doctors diagnose illness or injury.
  • The radiation used is given off by atoms that have large amounts of energy.
Test

Which of these is part of a radiographer's job?

Core concept

How does a nuclear power plant generate electricity?

Heat from radioactive elements turns water into steam, and the steam turns a turbine.

From fuel pellet to lit housePanel 1 / 5
1Press Next panel to follow the energy from the fuel to the house.
Press Next panel.
How does nuclear energy work?
Watch about 0:00 to 2:00 (timing is an estimate: check it once before the lesson)

Watch for: the point where the heat turns water into steam, and what the steam then does.

Open on YouTube

Blocked on your device? Open it here: How does nuclear energy work?. Nothing you are assessed on is only in the video. The five stages are all in the panels above.

Learn
  • Nuclear energy comes from the controlled release of heat from radioactive elements such as uranium and plutonium.
  • Heat from nuclear energy changes water to steam, which is used to move turbines to generate electricity.The last three steps are the same in a coal station. Only the source of the heat is different.
  • Nuclear energy is an alternative to using oil to generate electricity, especially in places that have no access to oil.For a country with no oil of its own, that is the whole appeal: electricity without having to buy fuel from somebody else.
  • Scientists are now trying to build smaller and more efficient nuclear power plants.Smaller plants would be cheaper to build and easier to place, which is why so much effort goes into them.
Key Facts
  • Nuclear energy comes from the controlled release of heat from radioactive elements such as uranium and plutonium.
  • Heat from nuclear energy changes water to steam, which is used to move turbines to generate electricity.
Test

What is the job of the steam in a nuclear power plant?

Interactive

Which settings give the most electricity without a shutdown?

You have followed the five stages. Now you are in the control room, and the heat that makes the electricity is the same heat that can shut you down.

Run the power stationlive
1Set the fuel rate and the coolant flow, then watch the core temperature, the output and the waste. Try to hold 500 MW for twenty seconds.
Run the power station
Two controls, three meters. The fuel rate releases heat into the core; the coolant carries that heat to the turbine, and the moving heat is what becomes electricity. Push too hard and the safety system shuts you down.

Your challenge: hold the output steady at 500 MW or more for twenty seconds without triggering a shutdown. Then find the highest steady output you can reach.

Core temperature: 20°C
Core temperature20°C
Electricity out0 MW
Waste accumulated0 units
Steady above 500 MW for0 s

This is a control loop, not reactor physics: real plants manage the reaction itself, not just a fuel valve. What is faithful is the trade: the same heat that makes the electricity is the heat that can shut you down, and the waste never goes down.

Watch for this: turning the coolant UP can raise the output, because electricity here comes from heat MOVED to the turbine, not heat sitting in the core. That is the steam doing its job.
Write it down

Find the coolant setting that gives the most electricity at 60 per cent fuel. Then record what happens to the output when you flood the core.

Core concept

What are the costs and risks of using energy from atoms?

Energy from atoms is used in nuclear power plants and in atomic bombs, and both carry serious consequences.

Learn
  • Energy from atoms is used in nuclear power plants and atomic bombs.The same understanding of atoms sits behind both. What differs is what people chose to build with it.
  • Accidents at nuclear power plants can result in the loss of lives and environmental pollution.When a plant goes wrong, the harm is not limited to the building or to the day it happens.
  • The use of atomic bombs can bring about destructive effects.An atomic bomb releases a very large amount of energy in a moment, and that energy is what causes the destruction.
  • Using nuclear energy requires careful use of the energy and proper disposal of nuclear waste.The waste stays dangerous long after the electricity has been used, so somebody has to look after it.
  • While there are benefits in using nuclear energy, there are costs and risks involved too.Both halves of that sentence are true at once, which is exactly what makes the decision hard.
Key Facts
  • Accidents at nuclear power plants can result in the loss of lives and environmental pollution.
  • The use of atomic bombs can bring about destructive effects.
  • While there are benefits in using nuclear energy, there are costs and risks involved too.
Test

Which statement gives the most complete picture of nuclear energy?
